title: Non-decreasing Subsequences
notes:
Task: Return all distinct non-decreasing subsequences of length at least two.
Idea: Backtrack through indices, appending a value only when it is at least the last chosen value; use a per-depth set to avoid duplicate branches.
Invariant: path is non-decreasing and contains only values chosen from the processed prefix.
Edge cases: Equal values may appear in a valid subsequence, but the same value is tried only once at each recursion depth.
complexity_reason: Backtracking explores subsequences and copies every valid result.

title: Non-decreasing Subsequences
notes:
Task: Enumerate distinct non-decreasing subsequences of length at least two.
Idea: DFS over later indices, choosing a value no smaller than the current path's last value and using a set per recursion level.
Invariant: The current path remains non-decreasing and index order is preserved.
Edge cases: Duplicate values can appear at different positions in one subsequence, but duplicate branch choices at one depth are skipped.
complexity_reason: The DFS explores candidate subsequences and copies every valid path.

title: Target Sum
notes:
Task: Count sign assignments that make the array sum to target.
Idea: Transform plus/minus assignments into selecting a subset with sum (total+target)/2, then count subsets with 1D DP.
Invariant: dp[s] counts subsets of processed values that sum to s.
Edge cases: If abs(target)>total or total+target is odd, return zero; descending updates ensure each number is used once.
complexity_reason: Each number updates subset-sum counts up to the transformed goal.

title: Target Sum
notes:
Task: Count ways to place plus and minus signs to reach target.
Idea: Convert the problem into counting subsets summing to (sum+target)/2.
Invariant: dp[s] is the number of subsets of processed values that produce sum s.
Edge cases: An out-of-range target or odd sum+target has no solution; descending iteration prevents reusing an element.
complexity_reason: Each number updates all feasible subset-sum states in descending order.

title: Next Greater Element I
notes:
Task: Find the next greater value to the right in nums2 for each value in nums1.
Idea: Scan nums2 with a decreasing stack and resolve stack values when a larger value appears.
Invariant: The stack contains unresolved values in decreasing order; next maps resolved values to their first greater value.
Edge cases: Values without a greater element map to -1; nums1 values are assumed to occur in nums2.
complexity_reason: Each nums2 value is pushed and popped at most once; queries use hash lookup.

title: Next Greater Element I
notes:
Task: Return the first greater value to the right in nums2 for every nums1 query value.
Idea: Use a decreasing stack to record next-greater mappings while scanning nums2.
Invariant: Every popped value is resolved by the current value, which is its first greater value to the right.
Edge cases: Values left on the stack have no greater successor and default to -1.
complexity_reason: The stack resolves each nums2 element once and query lookups are expected constant time.

title: Diagonal Traverse
notes:
Task: Return all matrix elements in alternating up-right and down-left diagonal order.
Idea: Traverse each diagonal by its index sum, collecting cells along the diagonal and reversing every other diagonal.
Invariant: Each diagonal consists of cells with the same row+column sum and is emitted in the required alternating direction.
Edge cases: Empty matrices return an empty list; single-row and single-column matrices reduce to ordinary order.
complexity_reason: Every cell is visited once and each diagonal is temporarily buffered.

title: Diagonal Traverse
notes:
Task: Visit matrix elements in alternating diagonal zigzag order.
Idea: Group cells by row-plus-column diagonal index and reverse every other diagonal's collected values.
Invariant: Each matrix cell belongs to exactly one diagonal and is emitted once.
Edge cases: Empty matrices return an empty array; one-dimensional matrices preserve their natural order.
complexity_reason: Every cell is processed once and each diagonal is buffered for ordering.

title: Keyboard Row
notes:
Task: Keep words that can be typed using letters from one keyboard row only.
Idea: Map each lowercase letter to a row identifier and check whether all letters of each word share the same row.
Invariant: A word is emitted only if every character maps to the same keyboard row.
Edge cases: Matching is case-insensitive; empty words are not part of the usual input.
complexity_reason: Each word's characters are checked once and the keyboard mapping has fixed size.

title: Keyboard Row
notes:
Task: Return words whose letters all belong to the same keyboard row.
Idea: Use a fixed mapping from letters to row IDs and compare every character's row with the first character's row.
Invariant: A word remains eligible only while all processed characters share the same row.
Edge cases: Convert letters to lowercase before checking; the input contains English letters.
complexity_reason: Each character is checked once and the mapping size is fixed.

title: Find Mode in Binary Search Tree
notes:
Task: Return all values with the highest frequency in a BST that may contain duplicates.
Idea: Inorder traversal visits values in sorted order, so count consecutive equal values and track the maximum run length.
Invariant: prev, count, and best describe the current value's run and the largest run seen.
Edge cases: Multiple modes are retained when tied; TreeNode is supplied by the judge.
complexity_reason: Inorder traversal visits each node once with recursion stack proportional to height.

title: Find Mode in Binary Search Tree
notes:
Task: Find every value occurring most frequently in a BST with duplicate values.
Idea: Inorder traversal produces sorted values, allowing consecutive runs to be counted.
Invariant: count is the run length of prev and maxCount is the largest run encountered.
Edge cases: A new larger count clears prior modes; equal counts add another mode.
complexity_reason: Every node is visited once with recursive depth proportional to tree height.

title: Next Greater Element II
notes:
Task: Find the next greater element for every position in a circular array.
Idea: Scan two copies of the index sequence and use a decreasing stack of unresolved indices.
Invariant: The stack holds indices whose next greater value has not yet been found.
Edge cases: Only indices from the first pass are pushed; unresolved answers remain -1.
complexity_reason: Each index is pushed once and popped at most once despite the doubled scan.

title: Next Greater Element II
notes:
Task: Return the next greater value to the right, wrapping around the array if necessary.
Idea: Scan the array twice and resolve pending indices with a monotonic decreasing stack.
Invariant: The stack contains indices awaiting a strictly greater value.
Edge cases: Push indices only during the first pass; if no greater value exists after one full cycle, the answer stays -1.
complexity_reason: Each index enters the stack once and leaves it at most once.

title: Base 7
notes:
Task: Convert a signed integer into base-seven notation.
Idea: Repeatedly divide the absolute value by seven, collect remainders, reverse them, and restore the sign.
Invariant: Each remainder is the next least-significant base-seven digit.
Edge cases: Zero returns "0"; negative values receive a leading minus sign.
complexity_reason: The value is divided by seven repeatedly, producing one digit per iteration.

title: Base 7
notes:
Task: Return the base-seven representation of a signed integer.
Idea: Repeatedly take remainder and divide the absolute value by seven, then reverse the collected digits.
Invariant: The collected characters represent the number's base-seven digits in reverse order.
Edge cases: Zero is handled directly and negative values retain a leading minus sign.
complexity_reason: Repeated division creates one output digit per iteration.

title: Relative Ranks
notes:
Task: Assign medal labels to the top three scores and numeric ranks to the rest.
Idea: Sort original indices by descending score and write each rank string into the corresponding original position.
Invariant: The sorted index list gives rank order, while result positions preserve the input order.
Edge cases: Arrays shorter than three receive only the medal labels that apply.
complexity_reason: Sorting the indices dominates and the result array stores one label per score.

title: Relative Ranks
notes:
Task: Produce rank labels for scores while preserving original athlete order.
Idea: Sort indices by descending score and place the rank label at each original index.
Invariant: The sorted indices enumerate athletes from highest to lowest score.
Edge cases: The first three ranks use medal strings; subsequent ranks are one-based decimal strings.
complexity_reason: Sorting indices takes O(n log n) time and the output and index array use linear space.

title: Most Frequent Subtree Sum
notes:
Task: Return every subtree sum with the highest frequency.
Idea: Compute each subtree sum in postorder and count its occurrences in a frequency map.
Invariant: A node's sum equals its value plus the sums of its left and right subtrees.
Edge cases: A null root returns an empty list; multiple sums may tie for maximum frequency.
complexity_reason: Each node is visited once and each distinct subtree sum is stored in the counter.

title: Most Frequent Subtree Sum
notes:
Task: Find subtree sums occurring most frequently in the tree.
Idea: Compute subtree sums in postorder, increment their frequencies, then collect sums tied at the maximum count.
Invariant: Each recursive return value is the exact sum of that node's subtree.
Edge cases: Null root returns an empty array; tied sums are all returned.
complexity_reason: Each node is visited once and subtree-sum frequencies are stored in a map.
